lede: Scento sorts perfume into 14 families, from Sunlit Citrus to Oud Court, each defined by the materials that lead the composition.

tree.name: Sunlit Citrus
tree.definition: Led by citrus peel and zest: bright, sparkling, cologne-clean openings that read as light and quick.

tree.name: Orchard Fruit
tree.definition: Fruit takes the lead, whether juicy, jammy or sun-ripe, from pear and peach to berries and tropical flesh.

tree.name: Green Leaf
tree.definition: Cut grass, leaves, herbs, tea and aromatic plants: cool, crisp, garden-air compositions.

tree.name: Petal Garden
tree.definition: Rose, peony, lily, freesia and other open-air blooms form the heart; fresh to lush, but not heavily creamy.

tree.name: White Bloom
tree.definition: Creamy, heady white flowers such as jasmine, tuberose, orange blossom and gardenia carry the structure.

tree.name: Powder Veil
tree.definition: Iris, violet, heliotrope, mimosa and aldehydes give a soft, cosmetic, powdery veil over the skin.

tree.name: Spice Route
tree.definition: Warm and sharp spices lead: pepper, saffron, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and ginger.

tree.name: Wood & Root
tree.definition: Dry, creamy or earthy woods and roots: cedar, sandalwood, vetiver, patchouli, oakmoss.

tree.name: Smoke & Leather
tree.definition: Leather, suede, tobacco, birch tar and smoke: dark, dry, tanned or fire-lit.

tree.name: Amber & Resin
tree.definition: Glowing amber accords, labdanum, benzoin, incense and myrrh: warm, golden, enveloping.

tree.name: Velvet Sweet
tree.definition: Edible warmth: vanilla, tonka, caramel, praline, coffee, cacao, honey and almond.

tree.name: Skin Musk
tree.definition: Soft musks and ambrette that smell like clean, warm skin or fresh laundry.

tree.name: Salt & Mineral
tree.definition: Sea air, salt, ozone, wet stone and mineral notes: airy, watery, coastal.

tree.name: Oud Court
tree.definition: Oud with rose, saffron, amber and incense: the dense, resinous style of Arabian-influenced perfumery.
